objects.name: building glazing system
objects.definition: A complete arrangement that retains one or more glass panes or manufactured glazing units in a frame, sash, door, channel or other support, including the necessary beads, gaskets, blocks, sealants and joints.
functions: Retain glass safely
Transfer glass actions to supporting construction
Control water, air and contact at the glass perimeter

ncc_references.relationship: Routes covered glazing either through Housing Provisions Parts 8.2 to 8.4 or AS 1288, depending on the assembly and application.

cad.pattern: One supported glazed field per scheduled pane or manufactured unit
cad.placement: Within a frame, sash, door, channel or designed support
cad.opening: Closes or divides an opening while preserving scheduled clearances
cad.load: Transfers face and edge actions through glazing supports

notes: The catalogue identifies physical parts but does not select glass thickness, type or support details from appearance alone.

objects.name: fully framed glazing assembly
objects.definition: A glazing assembly in which the glass is continuously retained or supported by a frame around all of its perimeter edges.
functions: Retain every glass edge
Distribute actions around the perimeter
Receive beads, gaskets or glazing seals

cad.pattern: Continuous retention on four edges
cad.placement: Inside a perimeter frame or sash

objects.name: partly framed glazing assembly
objects.definition: A glazing assembly where some glass edges are retained by framing and one or more other edges remain free, meet another pane or use a different designed support.
functions: Retain selected glass edges
Leave scheduled free or jointed edges
Transfer actions through the designed support pattern

cad.pattern: Explicit supported and unsupported edge map
cad.placement: At a documented frame or channel
cad.opening: Fills part or all of an opening

notes: A future tool must store the support condition of every edge; partly framed is not a visual style label.

objects.name: unframed glazing assembly
objects.definition: A glazing assembly whose glass is held by discrete fittings, clamps, pivots or engineered joints rather than a continuous perimeter frame.
functions: Retain glass at discrete points or edges
Keep exposed edges safe and finished
Transfer actions through fittings or joints

cad.pattern: Exposed glass edges with scheduled discrete supports
cad.placement: At floors, walls, doors or wet-area fittings
cad.opening: Glass forms the enclosure or screen
cad.load: Actions concentrated at fittings and joint supports

notes: Do not infer hole positions, notch geometry or glass type; these belong to an engineered or supplied assembly.

objects.name: butt-jointed glazing assembly
objects.definition: A glazing assembly in which adjacent glass edges meet across a narrow designed joint, normally with a compatible sealant and without a conventional mullion between them.
functions: Join adjacent glass panes
Maintain a controlled joint gap
Seal or structurally connect the meeting edges as designed

cad.pattern: Repeated panes separated by narrow glass-to-glass joints
cad.placement: Between end supports or around a corner
cad.opening: Joint gap remains explicit between panes
cad.load: Support depends on the documented framed, finned or structural-sealant arrangement

notes: An IGU butt joint needs a product-specific edge-support and weather-protection detail; it is not produced by simply butting sealed unit edges together.

objects.name: fixed glazed light assembly
objects.definition: A non-opening area of glazing retained directly in a main frame, door frame or screen frame rather than in an operable sash.
functions: Transmit light
Close a fixed part of an opening
Transfer glass actions to surrounding framing

cad.pattern: One stationary glazed field
cad.placement: Inside a frame bay

objects.name: glazed door side panel
objects.definition: A fixed glazed panel immediately beside a door opening and commonly sharing or abutting the door frame.
functions: Admit light beside a doorway
Close the area beside the door leaf
Provide impact-safe glazing where required

ncc_references.relationship: Glazing in side panels next to doors is treated as a human-impact location within the stated limits and exceptions.

cad.pattern: One fixed glazed bay beside the door leaf
cad.placement: Within or beside a door frame

objects.name: glazed transom light
objects.definition: A fixed glazed light above a door, window or lower glazed panel, separated by a horizontal frame transom.
functions: Admit light above an opening
Close the bay between transom and head
Transfer glazing actions to the transom and frame

cad.pattern: Fixed glazed field above a horizontal transom
cad.placement: Above a door, window or panel
cad.load: Supported by transom and perimeter frame

objects.name: glazed shower screen assembly
objects.definition: A fixed, hinged or sliding glass enclosure or screen at a shower, including panels, doors, channels, brackets, hinges, handles, seals and joints.
functions: Contain shower spray
Provide a transparent or translucent wet-area enclosure
Retain safety glazing and door hardware

ncc_references.relationship: Bathrooms and shower enclosures are identified human-impact glazing locations.

cad.pattern: Fixed and moving glass panels enclosing the shower edge
cad.placement: On a shower hob, floor, wall channel or bath edge
cad.end: Return wall or free panel edge
cad.opening: Includes door swing or slide and bottom drainage clearances
cad.load: Glass supported by channels, clamps, hinges or brackets

notes: The glazing model does not replace the separate wet-area substrate and waterproofing model.

objects.name: glass splashback panel
objects.definition: A glass panel fixed to a wall as a cleanable protective finish behind a basin, bench, cooktop or similar wet or soiling source.
functions: Protect the wall surface
Provide a cleanable finish
Bridge a prepared wall area with sealed edges and service cut-outs

cad.pattern: One or more wall-mounted glass panels
cad.placement: Against a prepared wall substrate
cad.opening: Cut around services and fittings only to approved geometry
cad.load: Adhered or mechanically fixed to wall

objects.name: building mirror
objects.definition: A glass product with a reflective backing or coating, installed as a wall-mounted, framed or otherwise supported reflective surface.
functions: Provide a reflected image
Form a durable interior finish
Remain safely supported if damaged where required

cad.pattern: Planar reflective panel
cad.placement: On a wall, cabinet or frame
cad.load: Supported by compatible adhesive, clips or frame

notes: A mirror is recorded separately because backing, adhesion and breakage retention differ from transparent glazing.

objects.name: insulating glass unit
objects.definition: A factory-made sealed unit containing two or more glass lites separated by one or more cavities and held apart by a perimeter spacer and edge-seal system.
functions: Reduce heat transfer compared with comparable single glazing
Provide a sealed cavity between glass lites
Combine selected glass products into one replaceable unit

cad.pattern: Parallel glass lites around sealed cavities
cad.placement: As one unit within a glazing rebate or support system
cad.opening: Factory-sealed cavity is not an open ventilation space
cad.load: Complete unit supported at documented setting and location blocks

notes: Model the IGU as an assembly when section detail or fabrication data matters; a simplified window tool may use only the overall panel envelope and make-up metadata.

objects.name: double-glazed insulating glass unit
objects.definition: An insulating glass unit made from two glass lites separated by one sealed cavity.
functions: Provide two glass layers
Enclose one insulating cavity
Accept different inner and outer lite products

cad.pattern: Glass-cavity-glass make-up
cad.placement: Inside a glazing system

objects.name: triple-glazed insulating glass unit
objects.definition: An insulating glass unit made from three glass lites separated by two sealed cavities.
functions: Provide three glass layers
Enclose two insulating cavities
Allow coatings and glass types to be scheduled by surface and lite

cad.pattern: Glass-cavity-glass-cavity-glass make-up
cad.placement: Inside a deep compatible glazing system

objects.name: laminated glass assembly
objects.definition: A manufactured glass make-up in which two or more glass plies are bonded together by one or more interlayers so broken fragments can be retained and other performance can be provided.
functions: Bond multiple glass plies
Retain fragments according to the selected product
Provide safety, security, acoustic, ultraviolet or decorative performance where specified

cad.pattern: Glass-interlayer-glass layered make-up
cad.placement: As a pane or lite within a glazing system
cad.opening: Solid bonded laminate, not a cavity
cad.load: Behaves as the selected laminated product

notes: Laminated does not automatically mean the selected product satisfies every safety-glazing location or structural application.

objects.name: glass pane
objects.definition: One cut piece of flat or formed glass, described by its size, thickness, glass product, processing, edgework and position within a glazing assembly.
functions: Form the transparent, translucent or opaque body of a glazed field
Transfer face actions to its supports
Receive coatings, printing, laminating or heat treatment

cad.pattern: One planar or formed glass body
cad.placement: Within a glazing system
cad.opening: Holes and notches remain explicit fabrication geometry
cad.load: Supported according to the glazing system

notes: Pane is the neutral single-piece term. Lite identifies a pane's position within an IGU or framed light and should be stored separately when that distinction matters.

objects.name: monolithic glass pane
objects.definition: A single thickness of glass that is not a laminated multi-ply make-up and is not, by itself, a sealed multi-lite insulating unit.
functions: Provide a single solid glass body
Receive cutting, edgework, heat treatment or coatings
Serve as one pane or one lite in a larger assembly

cad.pattern: One homogeneous glass thickness
cad.placement: As a pane or IGU lite
cad.load: Glass body carries actions to supports

objects.name: annealed glass pane
objects.definition: Ordinary glass cooled without the strengthening process used for heat-strengthened or toughened glass, so it retains its normal strength and breakage behaviour.
functions: Provide general glazing where permitted
Serve as feedstock for cutting, coating, laminating or later heat treatment
Break with ordinary annealed-glass behaviour

cad.pattern: Single glass pane
cad.placement: At a permitted glazing location or within another make-up

notes: Do not assign annealed monolithic glass to a human-impact location merely because the size fits the opening.

objects.name: float glass pane
objects.definition: Flat glass manufactured by floating molten glass on a bath to create substantially parallel, smooth faces, then supplied clear, tinted, coated or for further processing.
functions: Provide flat glazing stock
Transmit or modify light according to colour and coating
Serve as a base product for laminating or heat treatment

cad.pattern: Flat planar pane
cad.placement: As base or finished glass product
cad.load: Depends on final processing and support

notes: Float describes manufacture, not the final safety classification.

objects.name: patterned glass pane
objects.definition: Glass with a rolled, cast, etched or otherwise formed surface pattern that diffuses vision or provides decorative texture.
functions: Transmit light while obscuring detailed views
Provide a textured decorative surface
Serve as monolithic, laminated or processed glazing where compatible

cad.pattern: Planar pane with material texture or hatch
cad.placement: Within a glazing system

notes: Obscure is a vision effect; patterned identifies one way of achieving it.

objects.name: toughened safety glass pane
objects.definition: A glass pane heat treated to a high surface-compression state so it has increased strength and, when it fails as intended, breaks into many relatively small fragments rather than ordinary annealed shards.
functions: Provide a certified safety-glazing product
Increase resistance to mechanical and thermal actions
Limit dangerous shard formation according to its classification

cad.pattern: Finished pane with all fabrication complete before heat treatment
cad.placement: At a scheduled safety-glazing location
cad.opening: Post-toughening cutting and drilling are prohibited unless product evidence says otherwise

notes: Toughened safety glass and heat-strengthened glass are kept separate because their breakage classifications are not interchangeable.

objects.name: heat-strengthened glass pane
objects.definition: A heat-treated glass pane with strength between annealed and fully toughened glass and a different residual-stress and breakage pattern from toughened safety glass.
functions: Increase strength above annealed glass
Improve thermal-stress resistance
Serve in laminated or other designed make-ups

cad.pattern: Finished heat-treated pane
cad.placement: At a designed glazing location
cad.load: Strength and support selected by design

notes: Do not use heat-strengthened monolithic glass as an automatic substitute for a certified safety-glazing material.

objects.name: laminated safety glass
objects.definition: A laminated glass make-up tested and classified as a safety glazing material, using an interlayer intended to retain fragments after breakage.
functions: Provide certified safety glazing
Retain broken glass fragments
Remain as a barrier or sheet after breakage to the extent documented for the product

cad.pattern: Bonded safety-glass make-up
cad.placement: At a scheduled human-impact or other safety location

objects.name: toughened laminated glass
objects.definition: A laminated glass make-up whose bonded glass plies include toughened glass, combining the selected ply strength with interlayer fragment retention.
functions: Combine heat-treated plies with a bonded interlayer
Retain fragments after ply breakage
Provide the documented structural or safety performance

cad.pattern: Toughened ply-interlayer-toughened or mixed ply make-up
cad.placement: Within an engineered glazing assembly
cad.opening: Holes and notches coordinated before toughening and laminating

objects.name: wired glass pane
objects.definition: Glass manufactured with a wire mesh embedded through its body, historically used where breakage retention or fire-related performance was sought.
functions: Retain some fragments on embedded wire
Provide the documented product performance
Form a visibly wired glazed field

cad.pattern: Glass pane with embedded wire-grid representation
cad.placement: Only where the selected product evidence permits
cad.load: Supported according to documented glass design

notes: Do not infer current safety-glazing or fire performance from visible wire alone; identify the actual product and evidence.

objects.name: organic-coated safety glass
objects.definition: A glass product with a factory or approved organic coating system that enables the complete product to meet its stated safety-glazing classification.
functions: Retain fragments through a bonded coating
Provide the certified safety classification
Protect or decorate one glass surface where documented

cad.pattern: Glass body with one retained coating layer
cad.placement: At a location permitted by product classification
cad.opening: Coating continuity around cuts and edges follows product evidence

notes: Keep certified organic-coated products separate from after-market film until product scope and installation evidence are known.

objects.name: body-tinted glass pane
objects.definition: Glass coloured throughout its body by ingredients in the glass rather than solely by a surface-applied film or coating.
functions: Reduce or alter transmitted light
Modify solar heat gain and appearance
Serve as a base for laminating, coating or heat treatment

cad.pattern: Coloured glass material throughout pane thickness
cad.placement: As a pane or IGU lite

objects.name: reflective coated glass pane
objects.definition: A glass pane carrying a metallic or other optical coating selected to reflect part of the incident light or solar radiation.
functions: Modify solar heat gain
Change visible reflectance and transmission
Provide a designed facade appearance

cad.pattern: Glass pane plus a nominated surface coating
cad.placement: As monolithic glass or an IGU lite
cad.load: Glass support unaffected unless product data states otherwise

objects.name: low-emissivity glass coating
objects.definition: A thin factory-applied coating on a glass surface that reduces long-wave thermal emissivity and is positioned according to the selected monolithic, laminated or insulating-glass make-up.
functions: Reduce radiative heat transfer
Contribute to the scheduled U-value and solar performance
Remain protected on the product-compatible glass surface

cad.pattern: Zero- or thin-thickness material layer on one scheduled glass face
cad.placement: On the selected numbered surface
cad.opening: May stop short of an IGU edge seal where edge deletion is required

notes: Store the coating and the glass substrate separately so surface numbering survives pane reversal and IGU make-up changes.

objects.name: ceramic frit glass coating
objects.definition: A ceramic ink or enamel fired onto glass as a solid, patterned or dot coverage that becomes a durable part of the processed pane.
functions: Create opaque or patterned coverage
Provide decoration or bird/visibility patterning where designed
Conceal backing construction or modify solar performance

cad.pattern: Solid or repeated printed pattern on one glass face
cad.placement: On the scheduled processed-glass surface
cad.opening: Pattern may avoid vision or seal zones

objects.name: glass louvre blade
objects.definition: A narrow rectangular glass pane with finished exposed edges, retained at its ends by louvre clips or mechanisms and rotated with adjacent blades in an adjustable louvre window.
functions: Form one overlapping louvre blade
Rotate to open or close a ventilation slot
Shed water to the blade below when closed as designed

cad.pattern: Repeated overlapping strips at constant pitch
cad.placement: Between louvre jamb mechanisms

objects.name: unframed glass door leaf
objects.definition: A door leaf made primarily from a single safety-glass pane or laminated glass make-up, with exposed edges and discrete hinges, pivots, patches or rails instead of a perimeter door-leaf frame.
functions: Open and close a pedestrian doorway
Carry door hardware through prepared glass holes or notches
Provide an impact-safe transparent barrier

cad.pattern: One exposed-edge glass leaf
cad.placement: Within a doorway using patch fittings, pivots or rails
cad.load: Self-weight and use actions transfer through discrete hardware

notes: All holes and notches must come from the selected hardware and glass fabrication schedule.

objects.name: glass laminating interlayer
objects.definition: A polymeric sheet or cast layer bonded between glass plies to hold the laminate together and provide the selected fragment-retention, structural, acoustic, security, colour or solar function.
functions: Bond adjacent glass plies
Retain fragments after glass breakage
Provide product-specific performance
materials: cast resin or other documented polymer

cad.pattern: Continuous layer between glass plies
cad.placement: Bonded over the laminate area
cad.load: Transfers shear and retains fragments according to product

objects.name: insulating-glass lite
objects.definition: One glass pane occupying a defined outer, inner or intermediate position in an insulating glass unit.
functions: Bound an IGU cavity
Provide the scheduled glass and coating properties
Transfer pressure and support actions within the complete unit

cad.pattern: Parallel pane within IGU stack
cad.placement: Outer, intermediate or inner IGU position

objects.name: insulating-glass sealed cavity
objects.definition: The sealed physical space between adjacent glass lites in an insulating glass unit, containing dry air, another gas or a documented gas mixture.
functions: Separate adjacent glass lites
Provide thermal resistance
Contain dry air or gas within the edge-seal boundary

cad.pattern: Continuous void between two parallel lites
cad.placement: Inside the IGU edge-seal perimeter
cad.opening: Sealed, not connected to frame drainage
cad.load: Gas pressure interacts with lites and seals

objects.name: insulating-glass gas fill
objects.definition: The dry air, argon or other documented gas occupying an insulating-glass cavity as part of the manufactured unit's thermal make-up.
functions: Fill the sealed cavity
Contribute to thermal performance
Maintain the specified cavity atmosphere

cad.pattern: Volume equal to the scheduled cavity interior
cad.placement: Inside an IGU cavity

notes: Do not label every IGU as argon-filled; dry air remains a possible specified fill.

objects.name: insulating-glass spacer frame
objects.definition: A continuous or corner-joined perimeter spacer between adjacent glass lites that establishes the cavity width and forms the inner backing to the edge-seal system.
functions: Set the glass-to-glass cavity width
Carry or work with desiccant
Provide a perimeter base for edge seals

cad.pattern: Closed perimeter frame inset from glass edges
cad.placement: Between adjacent IGU lites
cad.load: Maintains lite separation and seal geometry

objects.name: warm-edge insulating-glass spacer
objects.definition: An IGU spacer made or configured to reduce heat conduction around the sealed unit perimeter compared with a conventional highly conductive metal spacer.
functions: Maintain IGU cavity width
Reduce perimeter thermal bridging
Support desiccant and edge-seal construction

cad.pattern: Perimeter spacer frame
cad.placement: Between IGU lites

objects.name: insulating-glass desiccant
objects.definition: A moisture-absorbing material placed within or associated with the IGU spacer system to keep the sealed cavity atmosphere dry during its service life.
functions: Adsorb residual moisture
Reduce internal condensation risk
Work with the sealed spacer and edge-seal system

cad.pattern: Granular or matrix fill within the spacer system
cad.placement: Inside or integral with the IGU spacer
cad.opening: Communicates with cavity through spacer system, not outdoors

objects.name: insulating-glass edge-seal assembly
objects.definition: The continuous perimeter seal system that bonds and seals the IGU lites around the spacer and protects the cavity from moisture and gas loss.
functions: Seal the IGU cavity
Bond glass to the spacer or secondary seal
Resist moisture entry and gas escape

cad.pattern: Continuous band around all IGU edges
cad.placement: Between glass edges and spacer perimeter
cad.opening: No gaps except documented manufacturing features
cad.load: Maintains unit integrity and cavity seal

notes: Frame drainage must protect this seal from prolonged moisture; the edge seal is not itself the window's external weather joint.

objects.name: insulating-glass primary seal
objects.definition: The inner low-permeability perimeter seal between an IGU spacer and glass lites, commonly forming the first barrier to moisture and gas transmission.
functions: Limit moisture-vapour entry
Limit gas escape
Seal the immediate spacer-to-glass interface

cad.pattern: Thin continuous seal along both spacer-to-glass faces
cad.placement: Immediately beside the IGU spacer
cad.load: Sealing rather than primary structural retention

objects.name: insulating-glass secondary seal
objects.definition: The outer perimeter sealant filling the space from the spacer toward the glass edge and providing mechanical integrity and environmental protection to the sealed unit.
functions: Bond the IGU lites around the perimeter
Protect the primary seal
Provide the documented mechanical and weather resistance

cad.pattern: Continuous outer perimeter seal band
cad.placement: Outside the spacer between IGU lites

objects.name: glazing bead
objects.definition: A removable or fixed linear profile fitted to a frame, sash or door to retain a glass pane, gasket or glazing unit against the opposite rebate face.
functions: Retain the glass or gasket in its rebate
Provide a replaceable finishing edge
Maintain the designed glazing bite

cad.pattern: Linear lengths around retained pane edges
cad.placement: In the frame or sash glazing rebate
cad.opening: Defines exposed glass edge and bite
cad.load: Retains glass against rebate under face actions

objects.name: glazing channel
objects.definition: A continuous U-shaped, pocketed or proprietary section that receives a glass edge together with gaskets, wedges, blocks or sealant.
functions: Receive and retain a glass edge
Provide required edge cover and clearance
Transfer glass actions to the support

cad.pattern: Continuous section along selected glass edges
cad.placement: Fixed to frame, wall, floor or ceiling support
cad.opening: Receives glass and seals within the pocket
cad.load: Transfers glass edge reactions through fixings

objects.name: glazing gasket
objects.definition: A resilient preformed profile placed between glass and its frame, bead or channel to cushion the edge, retain the pane and form a controlled seal.
functions: Separate glass from hard framing
Seal the glass-to-frame interface
Maintain pressure and glazing bite

cad.pattern: Continuous compressed profile around selected glass edges
cad.placement: Between glass and frame or bead

objects.name: glazing wedge gasket
objects.definition: A removable resilient wedge profile pressed into a frame or bead pocket to compress another gasket or directly retain and seal the glass.
functions: Lock the glazing gasket system
Apply controlled pressure to the glass
Allow glass replacement by wedge removal

cad.pattern: Continuous inserted wedge along glazed edges
cad.placement: In the frame or bead gasket pocket

objects.name: glazing tape
objects.definition: A preformed adhesive foam, butyl or elastomeric tape installed as a continuous glass-to-frame bedding, spacing or sealing strip.
functions: Cushion and space glass from framing
Provide a continuous seal
Hold the pane during assembly or as part of the documented retention system

cad.pattern: Continuous strip along the glazing rebate
cad.placement: Between glass and prepared frame or stop
cad.load: Bedding or retention only as documented

objects.name: glazing bedding seal
objects.definition: A continuous bed of compatible sealant or compound beneath or beside glass that cushions the pane, fills the rebate interface and forms part of the glazing seal.
functions: Bed the glass continuously
Exclude water and air from the rebate interface
Separate glass from hard frame contact

cad.pattern: Continuous shaped sealant bed
cad.placement: Inside the glazing rebate

objects.name: glazing setting block
objects.definition: A small resilient load-bearing block placed beneath a glass pane or glazing unit at designed locations to carry its self-weight and maintain clearance from the frame.
functions: Support glass self-weight
Maintain bottom edge clearance
Transfer weight to suitable frame support points

cad.pattern: Discrete paired or scheduled supports below glass
cad.placement: Between glass bottom edge and structural rebate support

notes: Do not substitute window-frame installation packers; the setting block supports glass inside the glazing rebate.

objects.name: glazing location block
objects.definition: A resilient block placed at a glass side or upper edge to maintain edge clearance, control movement or keep the pane positioned without serving as the primary gravity support.
functions: Maintain side and top clearances
Prevent glass migration
Keep the pane aligned during movement and service

cad.pattern: Discrete blocks at scheduled side or head positions
cad.placement: Between glass edge and frame pocket
cad.load: Locates rather than primarily supports glass weight

objects.name: glazing sealant joint
objects.definition: A shaped site- or factory-applied sealant joint between glass and frame, bead, channel or adjacent glass, sized and tooled for the documented sealing and movement role.
functions: Seal the glass perimeter or glass-to-glass joint
Accommodate documented movement
Protect the glazing pocket while allowing intended drainage

cad.pattern: Continuous tooled joint along selected glass edges
cad.placement: Between glass and retaining surface or adjacent glass
cad.load: Sealing role unless separately designed as structural silicone

objects.name: structural silicone glazing joint
objects.definition: A designed silicone joint that bonds glass to a supporting frame, fin or adjacent component and transfers specified structural actions in addition to sealing the joint.
functions: Bond glass to its support
Transfer specified face or edge actions
Seal the bonded interface

cad.pattern: Continuous designed bond line
cad.placement: Between glass and structural support

notes: A future tool may place a supplied structural-silicone detail but must not calculate joint dimensions or approve product compatibility from generic geometry.

objects.name: glazing bar
objects.definition: A linear frame member that physically divides a glazed field into separate panes and provides a glazing rebate, bead or seal on each side.
functions: Divide a large glazed field
Support adjacent pane edges
Provide fixing and sealing surfaces

cad.pattern: Repeated linear divisions between true separate panes
cad.placement: Within a frame or sash

objects.name: decorative colonial glazing bar
objects.definition: A narrow decorative bar or grille applied to one or both glass faces, fitted between IGU lites or clipped to a frame to imitate small-pane divisions without necessarily supporting separate panes.
functions: Create a small-pane visual pattern
Provide removable or permanent decoration
Align repeated bars across a window or door layout

cad.pattern: Repeated decorative grid over or inside one glazed field
cad.placement: On a glass face, between IGU lites or attached to frame
cad.opening: Does not create separate glass panes unless specified

notes: The true-versus-applied distinction changes pane count, IGU manufacture, quantities and section geometry.

objects.name: structural glass fin
objects.definition: A vertical or sloping glass member positioned roughly perpendicular to a glazed wall and used as a transparent structural support for adjacent glass panes through designed fittings or silicone joints.
functions: Support a glazed wall or panel edge
Transfer wind and self-weight actions to building supports
Maintain a visually transparent support line

cad.pattern: Deep narrow glass plate perpendicular to main glazing plane
cad.placement: Behind or at a glass-to-glass joint

notes: Exact make-up, dimensions and fittings are engineered and must not be inferred from facade height alone.

objects.name: glazing visibility marking
objects.definition: A permanent contrasting band, motif, dots or other visible marking applied to transparent glazing so people can recognise the presence of a door, panel or wall of glass.
functions: Make transparent glazing conspicuous
Reduce accidental human impact
Provide a repeatable visual cue across the required glass area
materials: durable applied marking or other documented system

ncc_references.relationship: Certain glass doors and panels capable of being mistaken for an opening require a contrasting visible marking.

cad.pattern: Continuous band or repeated motifs at the scheduled sightline
cad.placement: On the visible glass face

objects.name: safety-glass identification mark
objects.definition: A permanent etched, fired, printed or otherwise durable identification on a safety-glazing product that records the manufacturer or certification information required for the product's classification.
functions: Identify the safety-glazing product
Support inspection and traceability
Distinguish certified material from visually similar glass

cad.pattern: Small persistent mark near a nominated pane corner
cad.placement: On or within the safety glass product

notes: The mark records product identity; it is not the larger visibility marking intended to prevent people walking into transparent glass.

objects.name: glazing impact-protection rail
objects.definition: A horizontal rail, chair rail, transom or similar physical member placed across or in front of glazing to make it evident, intercept impact or divide the glass area as part of the documented safety arrangement.
functions: Provide a visible and physical cue at glazing
Intercept some human contact
Divide or protect the glazed field where the applicable detail permits

cad.pattern: Horizontal member across or immediately in front of the glazed field
cad.placement: Fixed to framing or adjacent supports
cad.load: Protection role depends on documented support and strength

notes: A rail is not an automatic substitute for safety glass; the applicable glazing path decides its permitted role.
